title: Alignment Incident
description: One alignment incident: an AI system behaving contrary to the intent of its developers, deployers, or users, or criminal-level human misuse of AI. One file per incident at data/incidents/<id>.yaml.

id.description: Permanent identifier, CVE-style: AID-<year assigned>-<sequence>, e.g. AID-2026-0001. The year is when the record was assigned, not when the incident happened. Sequence numbers increase within a year and are never reused. Must equal the filename. Use `npm run next-id` to get the next one.

slug.description: Human-readable kebab-case name used in site URLs, e.g. replit-agent-deletes-production-database. Unique. Can be changed; the id cannot.

title.description: Neutral, factual headline. Avoid sensational language.

date.description: When the behavior occurred, or was first publicly reported if the occurrence date is unknown. Use only the precision you can source: YYYY, YYYY-MM, or YYYY-MM-DD. Quote it in YAML.

status.description: confirmed: acknowledged by the developer/deployer, or documented in primary research with methodology. reported: credible public reports but no confirmation. disputed: credible sources contest the account. retracted: shown to be false; kept for the record.

actor.description: Who drove the behavior. model: the AI system acted against its principals' intent on its own. human-misuse: a person deliberately used the AI to do harm. Only include human misuse at a criminal level (assessment.criminality.likelihood of likely or above); sub-criminal misuse is out of scope.

models.description: Model ids from data/taxonomy/models.yaml. Use 'unknown' if the model is not disclosed.

organizations.description: Organizations involved, each with a role. ids from data/taxonomy/organizations.yaml.

role.description: developer: built the model. deployer: shipped the product where it happened. researcher: ran the study/eval that found it. reporter: first publicly reported it. affected: harmed by it.

behaviors.description: Behavior ids from data/taxonomy/behaviors.yaml. List the most central behavior first.

summary.description: One or two plain-text sentences for cards and listings. Every fact in it must also appear in `claims`.

writeup.description: Short-form write-up in Markdown, 1-4 paragraphs: what happened, why it matters, and what was done about it. Cite inline with [@source-id]. Every paragraph must contain at least one citation. No facts beyond what the cited sources support.

claims.description: Atomic factual statements, each backed by one or more sources. This is the evidentiary core of the record.

sources.description: Source ids from this file's `sources` list.

quote.description: Optional short verbatim quote from the source supporting the claim.

id.description: Short local id, unique within this file.

kind.description: primary: from the developer/deployer or the person who experienced it. research: paper, system card, or research write-up with methodology. news: journalism. social: social media post. analysis: commentary/blog analysis.

measurements.description: Quantitative findings reported by the sources, e.g. a misbehavior rate per model or the number of records deleted. The site charts these. Every value must come from the cited source exactly. Include them wherever a source reports numbers.

condition.description: The experimental condition or context, e.g. 'goal conflict + replacement threat, 100 samples per model'.

unit_label.description: Display unit when unit is 'other' or needs detail, e.g. 'records'.

model.description: Model id from data/taxonomy/models.yaml when the value is per model.

tags.description: Free-form tags for things not covered by the taxonomies (e.g. agentic, coding-agent, system-card).

assessment.description: Editorial estimates. These are the database's judgment calls, not sourced facts, and the site labels them as estimates. Each one carries a rationale that points back to claims or sources.

level.description: How far the behavior got. speculative: alleged, suspected, or inferred, but no instance directly observed. internal: observed only inside a controlled environment (lab research, evals, red-teaming, system cards, internal use) with no effect outside it. breakout: crossed the boundary of a controlled environment, e.g. escaped a sandbox, reached real systems or people beyond the test's scope, or leaked from internal use. deployed: happened in a released product or real-world use with real users and real stakes.

context.description: Optional finer detail on the environment.

severity.description: Real-world harm that actually occurred, not potential harm. none: no real-world harm. minor: inconvenience, embarrassment, small recoverable losses. moderate: significant financial, data, or reputational damage, or recoverable harm to individuals. severe: serious injury, death, or large irreversible losses.

categories.description: Harm category ids from data/taxonomy/harm_categories.yaml. Empty when severity is none.

monetary_damage.description: Estimated direct monetary damage in USD, as a range. Leave low_usd/high_usd null when there is no basis for an estimate. Use 0/0 when there was clearly no monetary damage.

criminality.description: How likely the conduct is criminal. For actor: model, judge as if a human had done the same thing. For actor: human-misuse, judge the human's conduct. charged and convicted are facts and need a source. This is an editorial estimate, not legal advice.

offenses.description: Plain-language offense names, e.g. extortion, computer fraud, wire fraud.

review_status.description: draft: not yet checked by a human against sources. reviewed: a maintainer verified every claim against its sources.
